pages.title: Anaemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan — revised guidelines

facts.text: Released by: Union Health Ministry at the 16th meeting of the Central Council of Health and Family Welfare
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: Shift: from prophylactic supplementation to testing, therapeutic treatment, Eating Right, digital tracking and Jan Chetna / Jan Bhagidari
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: Element: Beneficiary group; Added (7th): Low Birth Weight babies aged 0–6 months
Element: Intervention; Added (7th): Eating Right approach — iron-rich, diversified diets
Element: Institutional mechanism; Added (7th): Strengthened Monitoring and Evaluation framework
T3 → T4: Test, Treat, Talk + Track
IV iron therapy for severe anaemia / non-responders among pregnant and lactating women: Ferric Carboxymaltose, Iron Sucrose
Unified AMB Abhiyaan Portal integrates: JANANI (pregnant women), RBSK (child screening), U-WIN (immunisation records)
Anaemia Mukt Bharat launched: 2018 under National Health Mission — lifecycle approach
facts.head: Background

facts.text: WHO cut-offs: women of reproductive age Hb < 12 g/dL; children under 5 Hb < 11 g/dL
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Original interventions: IFA supplementation, biannual deworming (Albendazole), testing and treatment, food fortification, BCC, non-nutritional causes (malaria, fluorosis, haemoglobinopathies)
facts.head: Background

facts.text: ⚠ AMB gives prophylactic Iron-Folic Acid, not calcium; promotes delayed cord clamping
facts.head: Background

facts.text: NFHS-5 group: Children under 5; Anaemic: 67.1%
facts.head: Background

facts.text: NFHS-5 group: Adolescent girls 15–19; Anaemic: 59.1%
facts.head: Background

facts.text: NFHS-5 group: Women 15–49; Anaemic: 57%
facts.head: Background

facts.text: NFHS-5 group: Pregnant women; Anaemic: 52.2%
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Global: 40% of children 6–59 months, 37% of pregnant women, 30% of non-pregnant women 15–49
facts.head: Background

facts.text: WIFS: weekly supervised IFA for adolescent girls and boys + biannual deworming
facts.head: Background

facts.text: PMSMA: special antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month

pages.title: Hepatitis control — NVHCP and World Hepatitis Day

facts.text: World Hepatitis Day: 28 July
facts.head: Key facts

facts.text: National Viral Hepatitis Control Program (NVHCP): launched 2018 — covers A, B, C, D, E; free diagnostics and drugs; NVHCP-MIS portal
facts.head: Key facts

facts.text: Progress: 21.06 crore screened; 6.12 lakh Hep B and C patients treated; 1,153 treatment sites
facts.head: Key facts

facts.text: Seroprevalence (HIV Sentinel Surveillance 2021): Hep B 0.85% (1 in 118); Hep C 0.29% (1 in 345)
facts.head: Key facts

facts.text: Virus: A; Spread: Faecal-oral (food/water); Prevention: Sanitation
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: Virus: B; Spread: Mother-to-child, blood; Prevention: ⚠ Vaccine under UIP; birth dose within 24 hours
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: Virus: C; Spread: Unsafe injections, blood; Prevention: ⚠ No vaccine; cured by Direct-Acting Antivirals
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: Virus: D; Spread: Only in Hep B carriers; Prevention: Preventing B prevents D
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: Virus: E; Spread: Faecal-oral; Prevention: Sanitation; serious in pregnancy
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: A and E monitored via IDSP
facts.head: Virus types

facts.text: Hep B + C: about 1.3 million deaths/yr; 304 million living with infection
facts.head: Global
